Houston, if you found Leanne Morgan through Netflix’s *Leanne Morgan: Unspeakable Things*, this is your night.

Her stories come from family, marriage, getting older, and the little things at home that become a whole ordeal. She started doing stand-up in 2001, and she tells it like she’s catching you up across the kitchen table. I’d bring the person who laughs hardest at family group texts.

Houston, Nurse John taped his first special, *Against Medical Advice*, at the Alex Theatre this August.

He builds his set around hospital work, Filipino family dynamics, and the hard things healthcare workers carry home. Live, he performs in scrubs, works the crowd, and makes people feel seen. Bring the friend who has a shift story.

Houston, you may know Kev Adams from his Netflix special, *Kev Adams: The Real Me*.

He brings personal, close-to-home stand-up about love, success, and the strange parts of growing up in public. Kev started performing in 2009 and has played rooms from the Olympia to the Accor Arena. If you like comedy that feels honest without trying too hard, this is a good night to go.

Houston, Ellen Skrmetti, who appeared on *That Sounds Fun with Annie F. Downs*, is headed your way.

Her “Hey Jesus, It’s Me” sketches and live sets find the funny in faith, family, marriage, and midlife. She started stand-up in 2020, and her stories feel like the kind you hear around a kitchen table. I’d bring the friend who always has a comment after church.

Houston, if you know Corey Holcomb from *The Book of Coreythians*, you know he doesn’t soften the relationship talk.

He started in Chicago in 1992 and has spent years breaking down dating, conflict, and bad advice onstage. You may also know him as Boonie from *Black Jesus* or Robert Tubbs on *The Cleveland Show*. If you like comedy that is blunt and built around real relationship mess, I’d see this one live.
